articles.title: Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch Detail Tapping Into Dark Characters and Gaining Confidence at Newport Beach Film Festival
articles.summary: Get used to seeing these faces this awards season. Variety’s 2026 10 Actors to Watch took the stage in Newport Beach, California, for a conversation about performance, craft and process on October 18. Variety moderated this conversation in partnership with Newport Beach Film Festival.
body: During the conversation, Navarrette opened up about portraying Nikki and the challenge of developing a character since there is so little of the real Nikki in “Obsession.”

“It was really just my first opportunity where I kind of had the freedom, to a certain extent, to do whatever I could,” she said. “I really find the complication of Nikki to be what is the most beautiful about her. And I find people come up and they talk to me about her — specifically women — say, ‘That is a character that I find myself in.’ Of course people like to laugh, but I find that there’s a complexity, not just in women, but in us as people, where we are multiple people, and that’s beautiful.”
Jackson also spoke about the process of becoming his uncle, Michael Jackson, not just in his skills as a performer but also in his confidence.

articles.title: ‘Beast in Me’ Season 2 Casts John Goodman
articles.summary: John Goodman has joined “The Beast in Me” Season 2 at Netflix, Variety has learned. The second season of the series was announced in September, with Season 1 star Claire Danes set to return as Aggie Wiggs. Goodman will play Jack, Aggie’s father.
body: “The Beast in Me” was originally announced as a limited series when it was picked up in 2024. It also campaigned as a limited series at this year’s Emmy Awards, for which Season 1 star Matthew Rhys won the award for outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series. The series also won the Emmy for outstanding music composition for a limited or anthology series, movie or special (original dramatic score).

But in the tradition of “Big Little Lies” and other “limited series” before it, Netflix and “The Beast in Me” team began exploring the possibility of a second season and opened a writers’ room earlier this year.

“The Beast in Me” Season 1 showrunner Howard Gordon will serve as co-showrunner on Season 2 alongside Season 1 executive producer Daniel Pearle. Gabe Rotter is the creator and an executive producer of “The Beast in Me.” Danes will again executive produce in addition to starring. Antonio Campos, Caroline Baron, Amy Lippman, Conan O’Brien, David Kissinger, Jeff Ross, Claire Danes and Jodie Foster also executive produce. The series is produced by 20th Television.

The second season of the series was announced in September, with Season 1 star Claire Danes set to return as Aggie Wiggs.
“The Beast in Me” was originally announced as a limited series when it was picked up in 2024.

body: On Wednesday morning, Skydance CFO Dennis Cinelli (formerly Paramount Skydance’s finance chief ) sent a memo to staffers announcing the leadership team for the finance group — which will be intimately involved in trying to help the company achieve its projected $6 billion in annualized cost savings, an exercise set to include what are expected to be several rounds of layoffs.

“Today we’re announcing the leadership team for Skydance Finance. Each of these leaders brings the experience and judgment to help us build something exceptional, and I’m excited to work alongside them and to share where I think we can take this team from here,” Cinelli wrote in the memo, a copy of which was obtained by Variety.

Cinelli thanked employees who “put in extraordinary effort to support the acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery” and said that “your work was essential to getting this deal done.” He also gave a shout-out to the legacy Warner Bros. Discovery finance team, writing that “you kept the business performing through a long period of not knowing how this would end. That takes discipline, and it didn’t go unnoticed.”

articles.title: The Devils review – Ken Russell’s 1971 possessed-nuns tale is a frenzied aria of confrontation and hysteria
articles.summary: Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave put in the performances of their lives in this film originally banned for obscenity that highlights the violence of power. ‘I could never be Satan’s boy.
body: ‘I could never be Satan’s boy. I haven’t the humility.” The speaker is Father Urbain Grandier, the 17th-century French priest accused of witchcraft, stylishly played by Oliver Reed, in Ken Russell’s scabrous 1971 classic; it is now restored and rereleased in its complete form after years of censorship. It comes from an era when movies, playing in high-street cinemas, still had the power to shock, to position that shock in the polite cultural mainstream and to compel serious discussion about whether that shock – or, conversely, a ban – was justified.

Reed is a revelation with his intelligent, focused, charismatic and dignified performance as the sensualist cleric who submits to injustice like a dissolute version of Thomas Becket. Grandier is a magnetically handsome man and de facto municipal leader of the town of Loudun in western France, bullishly promoting its independence, its walls and fortifications; this is to the rage of Cardinal Richelieu (Christopher Logue) and the Catholic church, who suspect that it will become a sanctuary and power-base for Huguenots and Protestants.

articles.title: Film buffs love it. Trump and Tom Hanks hosted it. Can TCM survive a Hollywood mega-merger?
articles.summary: Since 1994, Turner Classic Movies has been a haven for old film lovers. Now with Skydance’s David Ellison calling the shots, fans are panicking over its unclear future. I have made many attempts to lessen the existential disaster we call Tuesday – tacos, trivia – but lately only one thing works.
body: Every Tuesday in October, Alicia Malone, an affable Australian film historian wearing business casual and a flippy bob, introduces a double feature. These are often midcentury melodramas featuring striking leads, serpentine plots, and the burnt hues of fall rendered in indulgent Technicolor. Like All That Heaven Allows (1955), about a widow who finds herself crushed under the weight of 1950s suburban conformity – and the teeny waistline of her swing skirts – while nursing a crush on her much-younger gardener. Or Leave Her to Heaven (1945), about a beautiful socialite so obsessed with her hapless husband that she will kill anyone who threatens their bond.

In these films, everyone has their original teeth and no one takes Ozempic. It’s my weekly break from doomscrolling, from whatever- maxxing, from the maddening norm of vertical content. I want to live in the world of Sweater Weather cinema all year long.

articles.summary: The entertainer gives evidence at his trial on charges including rape and assault, which he denies.
body: Russell Brand has told a jury that facing accusations of rape and sexual assault has been "deeply traumatic".
The entertainer told the jury at his trial that he has focused on the allegations "at the expense of my marriage, my children and my health".
Brand, 51, is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one charge of attempted indecent assault.
The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies all the charges.

articles.title: Post your questions for Alex Cox
articles.summary: As the cult director of Repo Man and Sid and Nancy prepares to release his final film, Dead Souls, he takes your questions. Everybody has their swansong, whether they know it or not.
body: If it really is his last film, the fiercely independent British film-maker can look back on a helluva run. He broke through with 1984 punk classic Repo Man, then went on to direct Gary Oldman as Sid Vicious in Sid and Nancy. He made the political “western” Walker in 1987, starring Ed Harris – then from 1988 to 1994 introduced viewers to cult and overlooked films as the original presenter of BBC Two’s Moviedrome, essentially doing film nerd YouTube decades before YouTube existed.

He ended up making films in Mexico in the 1990s, including the brilliant Highway Patrolman, then returned to his home town of Liverpool for Three Businessmen and The Revengers Tragedy. Back in the US Cox made Searchers 2.0 (an update of the classic western), Repo Chick (a sequel) and sci-fi comedy Bill the Galactic Hero.

articles.title: Government minister calls for review of 'unacceptable' BBC Scotland channel closure
articles.summary: The BBC announced the dedicated Scotland channel would move online as part of measures to make savings of £500m.
body: Culture Secretary Màiri McAllan has urged Ofcom to review "wholly unacceptable" plans to close the linear BBC Scotland channel.
The BBC last week announced the dedicated Scotland channel - as well as BBC Three and Radio 4 Extra - would move online as part of measures to make £500m of savings by 2028.
McAllan said moving the channel online would "reverse progress in improving the visibility and representation of Scotland within the UK's broadcasting landscape".
She called on Ofcom, the UK's independent broadcasting regulator, to scrutinise the decision and its implications.

articles.title: ‘It’s the gay Titanic!’ Inside La Bola Negra, the maximalist queer spectacular bound for Oscars glory
articles.summary: Oozing panache and bagging awards already, La Bola Negra is an eye-popping war and prejudice epic starring Penélope Cruz in a blond wig and Glenn Close speaking Spanish. We meet the ex-lovers who dreamed it up.
body: When Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo – the directing duo known in their native Spain as “Los Javis” – began writing their queer epic La Bola Negra, they weren’t thinking about whether it would be stylish (which it is) or win numerous awards (which it has) or capture what they refer to as “the anti-fascist zeitgeist” (which it does). Instead, they thought only of scale. “I’m done with LGBTQ+ movies being niche,” says Ambrossi. “I was like, ‘Let’s make the biggest, gayest war movie ever.’” Job done.

Throw in spectacular set pieces, Ken Russell-style visual flair, cameos from a blond-wigged Penélope Cruz and a Spanish-speaking Glenn Close, and the result is a maximalist collage where the Spanish civil war sits side-by-side with Grindr hook-ups. “We loved imagining scenes that you don’t usually have in queer movies,” says Ambrossi, citing the spectacular opening sequence in which a Spanish village is bombed by Italian fascists. “A lot of people have said they’ve been missing something like this. They want to buy popcorn and be given a big movie like Titanic.” His eyes widen. “This is the gay Titanic!”

articles.title: Mum quits job as lawyer to voice Netflix cartoon
articles.summary: Emily McGonagle, 42, decides to change careers after watching Peppa Pig and Paw Patrol on repeat.
body: A mum says she left her late-night legal career behind for voiceover work from home where she can care for her children.
Emily McGonagle started her working life as a lawyer in the capital, often finishing at 03:00, but started to question whether she could sustain it long term.
After having children, she decided to seek something "more flexible" than her daily commute from Colchester to Canary Wharf, and pivoted to voiceover work in 2019.
The 42-year-old voices eight characters for the children's television series Spike, which premiered on Netflix on 12 October and is its number one children's show on the site in the UK.
